title: The New Job Market: Hiring, Hunting, and AI in the Middle
description:
This session looks at how AI is reshaping every stage of the job hunt - from the CV that gets written, to the screening system that reads it, to the interview on the other side, to the market candidates are landing in.

The focus is practical and aimed at job seekers, career changers, and anyone trying to make sense of how hiring actually works now - but recruiters, hiring managers, and HR folks will get plenty out of it too.

We'll explore-

* The current challenges, specifically in the Auckland NZ marketplace
* Writing CVs and cover letters with AI - what works, what flags as generic, and how to keep your voice
* Getting past the bots - how applicant tracking systems and AI screeners actually evaluate applications
* The new interview landscape - AI-assisted screening calls, async video interviews, and live AI note-takers
* Interview prep with AI - mock interviews, company research, and rehearsing tough questions
* Where AI helps you stand out vs. where it makes everyone sound the same
* Job market shifts - which roles are growing, shrinking, or changing shape, and what that means for positioning
* Building an AI-resilient career - skills, signals, and portfolios that hold their value
* Spotting fake jobs, scam recruiters, and AI-generated postings
* Practical workflows and tools that are actually worth using

After these sessions we typically grab dinner nearby if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

description:

From May through to August we have planting days happening at reserves across:

Browns Bay
Torbay
Waiake
Murrays Bay
Rothesay Bay
Long Bay.

What is it? 
A community planting day where volunteers come together to plant native trees in local reserves. Every tree planted creates vital habitat for wildlife, stabilises coastal and stream edges, and enhances the natural beauty of the East Coast Bays for generations to come.
Who can come? 
Everyone is welcome - individuals, families, businesses and community groups of all ages and backgrounds. No experience needed.
What's involved? 
You'll be planting native trees and shrubs under the guidance of our team. Events run for 2-4 hours depending on the site. It's outdoors, active, and a great way to meet your neighbours and give back to your local environment.
What to bring:

Gardening gloves
A clean spade (if you have one - tools provided if not)
Water and snacks
Sturdy closed-toe shoes
Warm layers - it's winter!
And some locations (wetland planting) we recommend gumboots.

What's provided:

All tools and equipment
Native plants
Guidance and instruction throughout.

For full event dates, locations and to find your nearest planting day visit the Restore Hibiscus & Bays website.

description:

**Important Note for Attendees:**

* **The event venue entry will be closed at 6:30pm, please make sure you arrive on time.**

**Talk 1: From Zero Interviews to Real Projects: What to Build When No One's Calling Back? by Ismael Silva**
This talk is aimed squarely at where most of the room actually is right now — applying, waiting, wondering if the market has forgotten about them. The core idea is that waiting is the worst use of a junior's time, and there's a better way to spend those weeks that turns a CV into a portfolio and an interview into a conversation about something you've actually built.

The session will show that "building leverage" does not require massive side projects. It will also touch on the value of soft skills and leadership, making the discussion relevant for both junior and experienced developers.

**A bit about Ismael:**

* Ismael is a full-stack engineer specializing in Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, and Postgres, and currently runs a small product studio called Base Logic Labs. Before transitioning into tech, he spent more than 20 years in public speaking, sales, and leadership roles, delivering over a thousand talks across various settings.

Katrina meets a lot of ambitious young people who seem to believe that it's possible for them to advance in their careers at an aggressive pace (once they get their foot in the door). title: Lindauer Centenary: Talks with descendants and relations
location: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki, Wellesley Street East, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
To mark the centenary of Gottfried Lindauer’s passing on Saturday 13 June, the Gallery will be hosting two very special talks with relatives of Lindauer himself and sitter Paora Tūhaere.
Held in the beautiful Lower Grey Gallery underneath Ngā Taonga Tūturu, which features Lindauer’s paintings, these free talks are not to be missed. All are welcome but arrive early to avoid disappointment. More about the talks:

1pm: Nathan Pōhio, Kairauhī Matua, Toi Māori | Senior Curator, Māori Art and Ngarimu Blair, a member of Paora Tūhaere’s whānau, will discuss one of the portraits of Tūhaere, along with the place of portraiture in tikanga Māori and our exhibition Ngā Taonga Tūturu.
2pm: Jane Davidson-Ladd, Curator of Historical New Zealand Art, is in conversation with Michael Grant, the great-grandson of Lindauer, to further explore Lindauer’s life and legacy.

 Ā te Hātarei 13 o Hune, hei whakamahara i te rautau o te matenga o Gottfried Lindauer, kua whakaritehia e Toi o Tāmaki e rua ngā kauhau me ētahi o ngā uri o Lindauer rāua ko Paora Tūhaere, tētahi o ngā tauira.Toro atu ki ēnei kaupapa utukore, ka tū ki te Taiwhanga Grey, kei raro iho i Ngā Taonga Tūturu e whakaatu ana i ngā mahi peita a Lindauer. Kua tuwhera ēnei kaupapa ki te marea, heoi, me tae wawe mai kia whai wāhi atu. He kōrero anō mō ngā kauhau:

1pm: Ka whakawhiti kōrero a Nathan Pōhio, Kairauhī Matua, Toi Māori, rāua ko tētahi whanaunga o Paora Tūhaere, a Ngarimu Blair, mō tētahi whakaahua o Tūhaere, waihoki te wāhi o ngā whakaahua i roto i ngā tikanga Māori me te whakaaturanga, Ngā Taonga Tūturu.
2pm: Ko Jane Davidson-Ladd, Kairauhī, Toi Puri Mahara nō Aotearoa, rāua ko Michael Grant, te mokopuna tuarua a Lindauer, ka whakawhiti kōrero mō te oranga me ngā tuku ihotanga o Lindauer.
